title: On the structure of black hole interior in a model of scalar quasi-particles within the GR framework
abstract: We propose an effective, singularity-free model of the black hole interior described entirely by a scalar field with a non-linear self-interaction potential. The interior consists of three layers -- a core, a transition layer, and a crust -- each fixed by the local quasi-particle density and the corresponding extremum of the potential of the field. The crust is a layer of massive, positive-energy thermal excitations above the zero-potential well, beneath a genuine Schwarzschild horizon at $r = 2GM_{\rm ADM}$. The core is an AdS-type region of negative energy density, it simulates a condensate of quasi-particles which carry zero classical kinetic energy and form a negative potential well governed by a negative inverse temperature parameter. The two regions are joined through Israel matching across the transition layer, which sits at an approximately null-gravity hypersurface of maximal regular matter density and where both the sign of the energy density and the type of thermal excitations change. Solving the static Einstein equations, we obtain the metric and mass functions of each layer, the edge equation of state of the crust, the linear stability condition of the null-gravity surface for ordinary and effectively negative mass matter, and the two-temperature thermodynamics linking the kinetic excitations to the negative temperature ground state. The framework unifies core and crust within a single field description and highlights the role of the negative energy AdS core and the associated negative temperature notion in describing black hole interior. In this picture the formation and Hawking evaporation of a black hole appear as a quasi-static cycle of an almost adiabatic thermodynamic engine, with the negative energy core as the working substance.
summary: This paper proposes an effective, singularity-free model for black hole interiors using a scalar field description that results in three distinct layers: a core, a transition layer, and a crust. It treats the entire process of black hole formation and evaporation as a quasi-static thermodynamic cycle driven by negative energy within the core. The analysis relies heavily on solving Einstein equations and applying advanced concepts from statistical mechanics to describe matter states.
main_problem: To construct an effective, singularity-free model for the interior of a black hole by treating its structure as a thermodynamic system.
main_result: The black hole interior is modeled as a three-layered structure (core, transition layer, crust) whose evolution mimics a quasi-static, almost adiabatic thermodynamic engine cycle.
method: Solving static Einstein equations and applying WKB approximations to derive the energy-momentum tensor components for the various matter layers.
model_or_system: The model uses an effective scalar field with non-linear self-interaction potential to describe a three-layer black hole interior: a negative energy AdS core, a transition layer, and a positive-energy quasi-particle crust.
key_observables: Metric functions, mass functions $m(r)$, energy densities ($ho$), pressures ($p_r, p_\perp$), and the active Komar mass $M_{	ext{Komar}}(r)$.
important_parameters: Negative inverse temperature parameter ($ eta$) governing the core condensate; quasi-particle density; Schwarzschild radius $2GM_{	ext{ADM}}$.
main_assumptions: The system is treated as a static problem initially, and the process of formation/evaporation is modeled as an almost adiabatic thermodynamic cycle.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the radial ordering of the three layers ($R_- < R^+ < R_S$) and show the scalar self-interaction potential $V(\phi)$ across these regions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the physical system, deriving components using WKB approximations for the crust (leading to an isotropic EoS), analyzing stability near the null-gravity transition layer ($R^+$) via test particle motion, and finally framing the entire structure within a thermodynamic cycle analogy.
why_interesting: While focused on GR/BH physics, the core concept of modeling BH evaporation as a quasi-static, adiabatic thermodynamic engine—where negative energy acts as the working substance—draws strong parallels to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics treatments of open quantum systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic structure of the proposed black hole interior. The radial ordering is R−< R+ < RS: the inner AdS-like core with negative energy density (ρ < 0, p > 0) and its boundary-core shell are enclosed within R−; the transition layer (the ”factory”), which approximately coincides with the zero-gravity hypersurface Z : r = R+, attracts the regular matter from both sides and repels the negative-energy bubbles; the thermal positive-energy crust (V = 0) fills the region up to the Schwarzschild horizon at RS = 2 G MADM.

FIG. 2. The scalar self-interaction potential V (ϕ) of Eq. (3), plotted at m = M = 1 (with ϕ in units of M and V in units of m2M 2). The quasi-stable minimum at ϕ = 0 with V = 0 corresponds to the crust; the two symmetric negative minima at ±ϕ0 with V < 0 correspond to the negative-energy boundary core region; the barrier separating the wells is associated with the transition layer (”factory”).

FIG. 3. (a) Defect ratio δ = Rreg/R3L versus the density contrast ρcrust/ρcr, for several core fractions u = Rcore/R3L; the cube-root scaling and the δ = 1 reference (dashed) are shown. (b) The regular-BH match locus in the (u, ρcrust/ρcr) plane, separating the over-compact region (δ > 1, R3L < RS) from the defective/puffy region (δ < 1, R3L > RS).
